about.description:
Bmad has been developed at Cornell University's Laboratory for Elementary
Particle Physics and has been in use since the mid 1990s.
Bmad has a wide range of routines to do many things.
Bmad can be used to study both single and multi-particle
beam dynamics. It has routines to track both particles and
macroparticles. Bmad has various tracking algorithms including
Runge-Kutta and symplectic (Lie algebraic) integration.
Wakefields, and radiation excitation and damping can be simulated.
Bmad has routines for calculating transfer matrices, emittances,
Twiss parameters, dispersion, coupling, etc.
about.summary: Bmad is an object oriented, open source, subroutine library for relativistic charged-particle dynamics simulations in accelerators and storage rings.

raw_meta_yaml:
schema_version: 1

context:
  name: bmad
  version: "20260904-1"
  safe_version: ${{ version | replace("-", ".") }}
  build: 0
  # mpi variants get a build string so packages can depend on them explicitly:
  # `pkg * mpi_mpich_*` for mpich, `pkg * mpi_*` for any mpi, `pkg * nompi_*` for no mpi
  mpi_prefix: ${{ "nompi" if mpi == "nompi" else "mpi_" ~ mpi }}

package:
  name: ${{ name }}
  version: ${{ safe_version }}

source:
  url: https://github.com/bmad-sim/bmad-ecosystem/releases/download/${{ version }}/bmad_dist.tar.gz
  sha256: c7b0af248370d29f46c8148c7cae4524c4010068f525e5d3a94b833ee8bd49c9

build:
  # prioritize the nompi variant via build number
  number: ${{ build + 100 if mpi == "nompi" else build }}
  string: ${{ mpi_prefix }}_h${{ hash }}_${{ build + 100 if mpi == "nompi" else build }}
  skip:
    - win
  variant:
    # python is only a build helper (fix_rpath_macos.py) and a test runner;
    # nothing links against it, so don't build a copy per python version
    ignore_keys:
      - python

requirements:
  build:
    - ${{ compiler('c') }}
    - ${{ stdlib('c') }}
    - ${{ compiler('cxx') }}
    - ${{ compiler('fortran') }}
    - cmake
    - make
    - automake
    - autoconf
    - if: unix
      then: gnuconfig
    - libtool
    - m4
    - pkg-config
    - if: osx
      then:
        - llvm-openmp
        # Temporary fix for https://github.com/conda-forge/ctng-compilers-feedstock/issues/225
        - gcc_impl_osx-64 ${{ fortran_compiler_version }}.*
    - if: target_platform == "osx-64"
      then:
        - gcc_osx-64 ${{ fortran_compiler_version }}.*
    - if: linux
      then: libgomp
    - if: mpi == "openmpi" and build_platform != target_platform
      then: openmpi
    - python
  host:
    - readline
    - ncurses
    - cairo
    - pango
    - xorg-libxt
    - pgplot
    # `.*` is required by rattler-build's stricter match specs; conda-build
    # treated the bare `hdf5 {{ hdf5 }}` pin as fuzzy (e.g. hdf5 2 -> 2.*)
    - hdf5 ${{ hdf5 }}.* ${{ mpi_prefix }}*
    - xorg-libx11
    - xorg-xproto
    - fftw
    - openblas
    - if: linux
      then: libacl
    - libcblas
    - liblapack
    - lapack95
    - gsl
    - fgsl
    - libxraylib
    - if: mpi != "nompi"
      then: ${{ mpi }}
  run:
    - libblas * *openblas
    - openblas
    - pgplot
    - lapack95
    - fgsl
    - xorg-xproto
    - if: mpi != "nompi"
      then: ${{ mpi }}
  run_exports:
    - if: mpi != "nompi"
      then: ${{ name }} * ${{ mpi_prefix }}_*

tests:
  - if: build_platform == target_platform
    then:
      - script:
          - tao -help
          - python -c 'import ctypes.util; assert ctypes.util.find_library("tao") is not None'
          - python -c 'import ctypes, ctypes.util; ctypes.CDLL(ctypes.util.find_library("tao"))'
        requirements:
          run:
            - python

about:
  homepage: https://www.classe.cornell.edu/bmad
  license: GPL-3.0-or-later
  license_file: bmad/Copyright
  summary: Bmad is an object oriented, open source, subroutine library for relativistic charged-particle dynamics simulations in accelerators and storage rings.
  description: |
    Bmad has been developed at Cornell University's Laboratory for Elementary
    Particle Physics and has been in use since the mid 1990s.
    Bmad has a wide range of routines to do many things.
    Bmad can be used to study both single and multi-particle
    beam dynamics. It has routines to track both particles and
    macroparticles. Bmad has various tracking algorithms including
    Runge-Kutta and symplectic (Lie algebraic) integration.
    Wakefields, and radiation excitation and damping can be simulated.
    Bmad has routines for calculating transfer matrices, emittances,
    Twiss parameters, dispersion, coupling, etc.
  documentation: https://www.classe.cornell.edu/bmad/manual.html

extra:
  recipe-maintainers:
    - MichaelEhrlichman
    - hhslepicka
    - ChristopherMayes
    - ken-lauer
